entries.finding: A 2026 systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials involving 667 participants found a modest reduction in fasting blood glucose with Ashwagandha versus control, but heterogeneity was substantial and GRADE certainty was very low.
The 2026 Ashwagandha glycemic meta-analysis found the HbA1c estimate was imprecise and not statistically conclusive, so evidence does not support a firm HbA1c claim.

A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated randomized trials of Ashwagandha for endocrine outcomes, supporting continued investigation of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and gonadal-axis effects rather than a blanket hormone claim.

A 2026 three-level meta-analysis synthesized 13 randomized trials involving 599 participants to evaluate objective exercise-performance outcomes of oral Ashwagandha, with evidence concentrated in young adults and athletes.
The 2026 Ashwagandha exercise review noted that most available trials involved young adults or athletic populations, limiting direct generalization to broader adult populations.

A 2026 systematic review of 20 randomized studies involving 1,249 participants reported improved memory with Ashwagandha, while evidence certainty and botanical-reporting quality still require attention.
The 2026 Ashwagandha cognitive meta-analysis reported a small improvement in attention and processing speed, with low statistical heterogeneity for this outcome.

A 2026 GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluated curcumin for depressive symptoms and found evidence supporting a potential antidepressant effect, while certainty and clinical relevance should not be treated as equivalent to antidepressant therapy.
The 2026 curcumin depression synthesis explicitly used GRADE to evaluate certainty, making evidence certainty an important part of interpreting the observed symptom effects.

A 2026 dose-response meta-analysis of 34 randomized trials found curcumin or turmeric supplementation reduced fasting blood glucose in adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes compared with control.
The same 2026 meta-analysis found a reduction in HbA1c with curcumin or turmeric supplementation, although substantial heterogeneity across trials warrants cautious interpretation.
The 2026 curcumin/turmeric glycemic synthesis reported a significant reduction in fasting insulin versus control in adults with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes.
The 2026 meta-analysis reported a significant reduction in HOMA-IR with curcumin or turmeric supplementation, indicating an improvement in this surrogate measure of insulin resistance.
No significant change in HOMA-B was detected in the 2026 curcumin/turmeric glycemic meta-analysis, demonstrating that the pooled glycemic effects were not uniform across beta-cell-related measures.

The 2026 curcumin/turmeric dose-response analysis reported that efficacy varied by formulation and health status, reinforcing that curcumin products should not be treated as interchangeable interventions.

A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis specifically examined curcumin supplementation for body weight, BMI, and waist circumference in people with type 2 diabetes, providing population-specific evidence for body-composition outcomes.

In a 2026 GRADE-assessed synthesis of 34 randomized trials, saffron significantly improved Beck Depression Inventory scores but did not significantly improve Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores, showing outcome-measure dependence.

The 2026 saffron meta-analysis found improvement on the Beck Anxiety Inventory but no significant pooled effect on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, limiting claims of consistent clinician-rated anxiety benefit.
The 2026 GRADE-assessed saffron synthesis found no significant pooled effect on the Profile of Mood States measure despite significant effects on some self-reported depression and anxiety scales.

The 2026 saffron depression analysis showed very high statistical heterogeneity for Beck Depression Inventory results, so the pooled effect should not be interpreted as a uniform response across all trials.
The 2026 saffron anxiety analysis also showed very high heterogeneity for Beck Anxiety Inventory results, highlighting uncertainty around the size of benefit between studies.

A systematic review of randomized trials reported preliminary evidence that saffron may improve sleep duration and sleep quality, but the evidence base consisted of only five trials and 379 participants.

A 2026 umbrella review covering 36 publications, 296 trials, and 43,570 participants found ginger supplementation was consistently associated with reductions in C-reactive protein across included meta-analyses.

The 2026 ginger umbrella review found consistent reductions in interleukin-6 across included meta-analyses, supporting an anti-inflammatory biomarker signal rather than a direct disease-treatment claim.
The 2026 umbrella review reported improvements in several oxidative-stress and antioxidant-status measures, including malondialdehyde, glutathione peroxidase, and total antioxidant capacity.
